statements.statement_en: The Jewish character of the state should be anchored more firmly in law, even if non-Jewish citizens feel less equal.
Yeshiva students should be drafted into the army or civilian service, even if this forces them to give up full-time Torah study.
Tuition aid, daycare, tax breaks and land should go first to those who did military or national service, even if others get less.
Much more housing construction should be allowed, even at the cost of building on open spaces and greater strain on infrastructure.
The state should expand legal protections and equal rights for LGBT people, even if religious citizens and businesses must sometimes act against their beliefs.
Measures against terrorists and their supporters should be harsher, such as the death penalty or revoking citizenship, even if uninvolved people are affected.
Suspects and defendants should have fewer legal protections during arrest, questioning and trial, even if the risk of convicting innocent people grows.
The Supreme Court should have less power to cancel laws and government decisions, even if citizens have fewer ways to challenge them in court.
